title: Closed pushforward compares base-change ranges
statement: Let $p:X\to S$, $g:T\to S$ be scheme morphisms, $q\in\mathbb Z$, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $x\in X$. Use the canonical source and target stalks $A(U),B(U)$, maps $b_U:A(U)\to B(U)$, and restrictions $r_\varphi$ of [def-sbc-canonical-base-change-stalk-transitions]. Let $f:T'\to T$, let $i:Z\to T'$ be a closed immersion, and let $\zeta\in B(T')$. Write $F'=f^*F$, $Y'=T'\times_S X$, with projections $e':Y'\to T'$ and $h':Y'\to X$. If $r_i(\zeta)\in\operatorname{im}(b_Z)$, then the image of $\zeta$ under the target-functor coefficient map induced by the unit $F'\to i_*i^*F'$ belongs to the stalkwise image of the degree-$q$ base-change map for the square $Y'$ and coefficient $i_*i^*F'$ [sbc-def-base-change-map].

proof.text: Use the closed-coefficient source transition isomorphism [lem-sbc-closed-coefficient-source-transition-iso] and target transition isomorphism [lem-sbc-closed-coefficient-target-transition-iso]. These are the two geometric parts of the closed-pushforward comparison.

Use coefficient naturality [lem-sbc-target-coefficient-transition-naturality] and the existing base-change coefficient-naturality and transition-pasting identities [sbc-def-base-change-map]. These provide the two commuting stalk diagrams.

Pass both commuting diagrams to the geometric stalk. Transport a preimage by the inverse source transition and cancel the injective target transition. Cancel the coefficient pullback isomorphism with its inverse-hom identity. Specialize the general square argument directly to the canonical pullbacks over f≫g and (i≫f)≫g. Associativity proves the canonical lift commutes, and the inverse-image composition isomorphism identifies (i≫f)^*F with i^*f^*F. No replacement of canonical pullback objects or equality transport of range sets is needed.
